comparison.stem: A valid Massachusetts doxycycline prescription for a chlamydia partner uses 'EPT' in place of the partner's name and address. The pharmacist will dispense it. Which record setup is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a separate profile and prescription label using the EPT designation in place of the partner name/address.
Place the partner's doxycycline under the index patient's profile as an extra refill.
Dispense the drug with no profile or label because the partner is unnamed.
Invent a partner date of birth and legal name to make the software accept the prescription.
Convert doxycycline to OTC status for this transaction.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is deciding how to package several daily medications for one patient. Which statements correctly apply the Schedule II/III rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A stable maintenance classification permits a Schedule II drug to share a multi-drug single-dose pouch.
A licensee may not dispense a Schedule II or III controlled substance in a multi-drug single-dose package.
That prohibition does not by its own terms ban a single-drug single-dose package.
Every form of compliance packaging is prohibited for every Schedule II or III controlled substance.
The policy phrase 'unless otherwise prohibited' preserves the regulatory Schedule II/III restriction.

comparison.stem: A referred patient at a Massachusetts retail pharmacy has run out of a medication her supervising physician prescribed, and the physician is unreachable. The collaborating pharmacist has never dispensed this patient a different medication for the same condition. What may the pharmacist do under the retail collaborative power?

choices.text: Initiate an equivalent medication for the same condition for up to 30 days.
Extend the current therapy the supervising physician prescribed by 30 days.
Extend the current therapy indefinitely until the physician can be reached.
Substitute a therapeutically similar agent and notify the physician afterwards.
Nothing, because the retail setting confers no continuation power at all.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician's license has been expired for 26 months. The technician submits the renewal form and fees, but the Board has not renewed the license or decided whether to impose additional conditions. The pharmacy wants the technician to begin work under direct pharmacist supervision. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: Submitting the form and fees restores the license provisionally while the Board reviews the application.
Direct pharmacist supervision may permit practice during the renewal review despite the expired license.
A lapse exceeding two years automatically requires a specified national technician examination before renewal.
The technician cannot practice until renewal; because the lapse exceeded two years, additional Board conditions may apply.
A lapse exceeding two years permanently bars renewal of the technician license.

comparison.stem: A known Massachusetts prescriber telephones a new warfarin prescription to the pharmacist. Warfarin is a Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription drug. Which actions correctly apply to this oral prescription? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Because Schedule VI is excluded from §20(c)'s later follow-up-prescription requirement, the pharmacist does not need to create an oral-prescription record.
The pharmacist should immediately reduce the oral prescription to writing with the information required by Massachusetts law.
The pharmacist must demand a replacement electronic prescription within two days because §20(c) applies identically to Schedule VI.
The Schedule VI exception from the later follow-up document does not eliminate the pharmacist's ordinary authenticity and validity responsibilities.
The pharmacist must convert the prescription to Schedule V before an oral transmission can be accepted.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing a new prescription for delivery to a patient's home. To satisfy the counseling-offer requirement for off-site delivery, the pharmacy provides access to its toll-free service that connects the patient with a pharmacist. Before the prescription is sent, which additional step is required under Massachusetts law?

choices.text: Print the toll-free service number on a label affixed to each prescription drug container.
Place the number only on the outer shipping package, as long as it remains visible until opening.
Include the number only on the delivery receipt that the patient signs.
Send the number in an electronic message after the package has been delivered.
Replace the toll-free number with the dispensing pharmacy's ordinary local number on the container label.

comparison.stem: A pharmacy system sees ‘Massachusetts Schedule VI’ on a gabapentin record and automatically applies federal Schedule II ordering rules and federal Schedule III-V refill limits. Which correction is most accurate?

choices.text: Keep the federal flags because every Massachusetts Schedule VI drug is also a federal Schedule II drug.
Remove all prescription controls because Schedule VI means over-the-counter under federal law.
Do not import federal Schedule II or III-V controls solely from Massachusetts Schedule VI status; determine federal scheduling separately.
Convert gabapentin to federal Schedule IV whenever it is dispensed in Massachusetts.
Apply federal Form 222 ordering to every Massachusetts prescription drug that is not listed in federal Schedules III-V.

comparison.stem: A pharmacist receives a facially complete controlled-substance prescription but identifies unresolved facts strongly suggesting it may not have been issued for a legitimate medical purpose. The prescriber has a valid DEA registration. What is the pharmacist's federal responsibility?

choices.text: Dispense after confirming the DEA number because registration establishes the prescriber's responsibility for medical purpose.
Resolve the red flags before dispensing; unresolved legitimacy concerns require declining the fill.
Dispense the first fill, document the concerns, and investigate the red flags before the next dispensing.
Change the quantity or directions to a safer-looking regimen without contacting the prescriber, then dispense.
Transfer the final validity decision to a technician who reviewed the patient's profile and identification.

comparison.stem: Under current Massachusetts Policy 2024-05, which Schedule II/III prescriptions may qualify for up to a 90-day supply when otherwise lawful? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Testosterone cypionate replacement therapy
Buprenorphine for opioid use disorder
Oxycodone for ordinary outpatient pain
Methylphenidate for a non-opioid indication
Lisdexamfetamine for ADHD

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee is performing data-entry work while a pharmacist is directly supervising the trainee. At pickup, the patient asks whether the new medication can be taken with warfarin, and the profile shows an unresolved DUR alert. Which actions are appropriate for the trainee? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Collect and enter nonclinical demographic information while remaining under direct pharmacist supervision.
Counsel the patient on the interaction after reading the drug-information screen.
Perform authorized prescription-processing and staging tasks under direct pharmacist supervision, while leaving final verification to the pharmacist.
Continue other authorized clerical or technical trainee functions while under direct pharmacist supervision.
Refer the clinical question and unresolved DUR issue to the pharmacist rather than exercising pharmacist professional judgment.

comparison.stem: A community pharmacy fills a patient-specific midazolam prescription for home use. The claim is cash-paid and the drug is not an opioid. What should the pharmacist do about MassPAT?

choices.text: Report the dispensing because it is Schedule IV.
Exclude it because the claim was paid in cash.
Exclude it because midazolam is not an opioid.
Report only if more than seven days are supplied.
Submit it with the pharmacy's inventory report at month-end.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts patient collects a refill of an anticoagulant after a recent dose change communicated by the prescriber. A technician tells the pharmacist that counseling is not required because the prescription is a refill rather than a new drug therapy. How should the pharmacist respond?

choices.text: Agree, because the counseling duty attaches only to a prescription for new drug therapy.
Agree, provided the patient was counseled when this drug was first dispensed to her.
Agree, unless the patient affirmatively requests counseling from the pharmacist at pickup.
Disagree, because every refill of any prescription requires counseling without exception.
Disagree, because counseling is also required where the therapy is significant for the patient's health and safety.

comparison.stem: A pharmacy dispenses a drug for which FDA requires a Medication Guide. The patient accepts the printed material but declines to discuss the medication with the pharmacist. Which statements are correct? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The counseling refusal permits the pharmacy to omit the Medication Guide when the guide would otherwise be required.
The required Medication Guide still must be provided even though the patient declines verbal discussion.
Handing over the Medication Guide automatically proves that every Massachusetts counseling requirement has been satisfied.
The federal patient-document duty and the Massachusetts counseling duty should be evaluated as separate requirements.
Medication Guides are limited to drugs that are federally scheduled controlled substances.

comparison.stem: A patient presents a valid clozapine prescription in August 2026. A pharmacist trained under the former Clozapine REMS tells a colleague that the pharmacy cannot dispense until the patient is enrolled in the REMS and an ANC result is entered into that program. What is the current federal position?

choices.text: The former REMS enrollment and ANC-verification gate remains mandatory for every clozapine dispensing.
The pharmacy may ignore any clinically significant blood-count information because removal of the REMS ended all clozapine monitoring concerns.
The pharmacy must enroll only the prescriber, while pharmacy and patient enrollment are no longer required.
FDA removed the Clozapine REMS, so REMS enrollment and REMS ANC verification are no longer federal dispensing prerequisites, although clinical monitoring remains relevant.
Clozapine became an over-the-counter drug when the REMS was removed.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is counseling a patient on a new inhaled therapy. Which items does the regulation identify as information counseling may include? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacy's wholesale acquisition cost for the medication.
Special directions and instructions for preparation, administration and use by the patient.
Techniques for self-monitoring drug therapy.
Proper storage and disposal of the medication.
Action to be taken in the event of a missed dose or adverse reaction.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy audits its ADD program. Which records or data should be retained as part of the ADD record system? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A verbal recollection from the charge nurse instead of a retrievable transaction record
Documentation of required approval for the ADD location
ADD transaction data showing product, patient identifier, date/time, and reconciliation
Records of ADD maintenance and personnel access/events
Retain retrievable ADD records for at least two years as required by the device policy.

comparison.stem: An adult patient receives a lawful 14-day outpatient prescription for buprenorphine-naloxone specifically for treatment of opioid use disorder. A staff member says Massachusetts' seven-day initial-opiate statute automatically requires the prescription to be reduced to seven days. What is the best response to that specific claim?

choices.text: Agree, because every medication related to an opioid is subject to the seven-day statute regardless of indication.

Disagree. The seven-day statute expressly does not apply to medications designed for treatment of substance abuse or opioid dependence; the prescription must instead satisfy the other laws governing its OUD pathway.
Agree unless the patient has previously filled an opioid prescription in Massachusetts.
Disagree because buprenorphine-naloxone becomes Massachusetts Schedule VI when used for OUD.
Reduce the quantity to seven days without prescriber involvement because pharmacists may unilaterally rewrite any opioid prescription to comply with supply limits.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy uses one ADD only as an approved emergency medication kit and a second ADD for routine medication dispensing. A licensed nurse asks to load both machines. Which answer best applies under the current ADD policy?

choices.text: The nurse may load the emergency-kit ADD; routine-dispensing ADD loading is limited to certified technicians or interns under pharmacist supervision.
The nurse may load both machines because the same pharmacy owns both devices and supervises the medication inventory.
The nurse may load neither machine because routine and emergency ADDs are restricted to pharmacists and pharmacy interns.
The nurse may load the routine machine whenever it contains only Schedule VI medications and no federally controlled drugs.
Both machines use the emergency-kit loader list as long as they are located inside the same Massachusetts retail pharmacy.

comparison.stem: At one Massachusetts pharmacy a patient refuses to give any allergy history after being asked on three separate visits. At another, a patient is never asked because the queue is long. Both patient profiles are incomplete in exactly the same respect. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both pharmacies are compliant, because the standard is only reasonable effort.
Both pharmacies are in breach, because the profile has to be complete.
Compliance turns on whether the missing history was clinically significant.
The first pharmacy made a reasonable effort and is compliant on these facts.
The second pharmacy made no effort at all and is not compliant.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy uses one ADD only as an approved emergency medication kit and a second ADD for routine medication dispensing. A licensed nurse asks to load both machines. Which answer best applies under the current ADD policy?

choices.text: The nurse may load the emergency-kit ADD; routine-dispensing ADD loading is limited to certified technicians or interns under pharmacist supervision.
The nurse may load both machines because the same pharmacy owns both devices and supervises the medication inventory.
The nurse may load neither machine because routine and emergency ADDs are restricted to pharmacists and pharmacy interns.
The nurse may load the routine machine whenever it contains only Schedule VI medications and no federally controlled drugs.
Both machines use the emergency-kit loader list as long as they are located inside the same Massachusetts retail pharmacy.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee working under the direct supervision of a pharmacist is asked to answer the pharmacy telephone during a staffing crunch and take a new prescription from a prescriber's agent. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The trainee may take the prescription while under direct supervision.
The trainee may take the prescription if the pharmacist listens on a second handset.
The trainee may take the prescription if it is for a Schedule VI drug.
The trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone.
The trainee may take the prescription after 500 hours of trainee employment.

comparison.stem: An applicant for a Massachusetts pharmacy technician licence is 19, holds a high school diploma, is of good moral character and has no drug-related felony. Which of the following, standing alone, satisfies the remaining eligibility requirement? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Certification conferred by a Board-approved certifying body.
A substantially equivalent pharmacy technician licence in good standing in another state.
A Board-approved passing score on a Board-approved assessment examination taken after completing a Board-approved training program.
Twelve months of employment as a pharmacy cashier in a licensed pharmacy.
A letter from the employing Manager of Record attesting to the applicant's competence.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts supervising physician refers a patient for collaborative drug therapy management, records the referral and the patient's consent in his own chart, and tells the collaborating pharmacist that the documentation is complete and nothing further is needed. Where must the individual referral and consent be recorded?

choices.text: In the supervising physician's record alone, which is what the statute requires.
In the pharmacist's record alone, since the pharmacist delivers the service.
In whichever of the two records the professionals agree should hold them.
In the patient's record, by the pharmacist and by the supervising physician.
In a register filed with the Board, separately from the patient's record.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist discloses nothing about any patient to anyone. Completed prescriptions sit face up on an open counter and a printed waiting list showing patient names is visible to everyone standing in the queue. No one is shown to have read either of them. What is the position?

choices.text: Compliant, because the pharmacist made no disclosure to any third party.
Compliant, because no one is shown to have read the information on display.
Compliant, provided the pharmacy makes a private consultation area available.
In breach, but only once a patient complains about the arrangement.
In breach, because the duty includes protecting confidential information.

comparison.stem: A pharmacy is preparing medications for an ADD at a Massachusetts health care facility. Which actions are consistent with the current ADD policy? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Load a manufacturer's sealed original single-dose package when suitable
Use medication repackaged according to professional standards for a single dose or person
Report medication losses according to the pharmacy licensing body's requirements
Use single-dose or person-specific packaging that preserves medication identity and traceability.
Ignore a documented shortage if all missing doses are Schedule VI

comparison.stem: A community pharmacy fills a patient-specific midazolam prescription for home use. The claim is cash-paid and the drug is not an opioid. What should the pharmacist do about MassPAT?

choices.text: Report the dispensing because it is Schedule IV.
Exclude it because the claim was paid in cash.
Exclude it because midazolam is not an opioid.
Report only if more than seven days are supplied.
Submit it with the pharmacy's inventory report at month-end.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist administers an eligible patient-specific long-acting antipsychotic under the current MH/SUD pathway. Which workflow principles are consistent with the guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Send the administration record to the prescriber as soon after administration as practical, as strongly encouraged by DCP guidance
Allow a cashier to perform the injection after the pharmacist verifies the prescription
Skip privacy protections because the medication treats mental illness
Use a prescribed single dose supplied in eligible single-dose packaging
Document the administration in the pharmacy's patient record

comparison.stem: During prospective drug utilization review, the pharmacy system flags a clinically significant conflict. A certified pharmacy technician tells the pharmacist that the technician can clear the alert under the pharmacy's protocol and that documentation is needed only if the prescriber is called. Which statements correctly describe the Massachusetts requirements? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist must determine what measures are appropriate in response to the DUR finding and may choose consultation with the prescriber, the patient, or the patient's agent when appropriate.
The pharmacist must document the measures taken in response to the DUR finding, not only a prescriber call.
A certified pharmacy technician may resolve the clinical conflict independently when an approved protocol supplies the decision steps.
Every DUR finding requires prescriber consultation before dispensing, regardless of the pharmacist's clinical assessment.
Documentation is optional when the pharmacist addresses the issue directly with the patient rather than the prescriber.

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist completes the screening and issues a prescription for a hormonal contraceptive patch on a Friday afternoon. She tells the patient the pharmacy will order the product and asks her to return the following week to collect it, although an equivalent product is in stock. Is that consistent with the statute?

choices.text: Yes, because the prescribing duty and the dispensing decision are separate.
Yes, because the patient suffers no clinical detriment from a short wait.
Yes, provided the pharmacist gives the patient the written record on the Friday.
No, because the statute requires dispensing as soon as practicable after issuing.
No, because a pharmacist may not issue a prescription she cannot fill that day.

comparison.stem: A prescriber telephones a pharmacy about a drug for which FDA requires a Medication Guide. She has concluded that receiving the Guide would not be in this particular patient's best interest, and directs that it not be provided. At the counter the patient asks the pharmacist for written information about the medicine. What must the pharmacist do?

choices.text: Provide the Medication Guide, because the patient has requested information.
Withhold the Guide but supply the manufacturer's patient information leaflet instead.
Withhold the Guide, because the prescriber's clinical direction controls at the counter.
Withhold the Guide unless the patient puts the request in writing.
Contact the prescriber for permission before providing anything in writing.

comparison.stem: An eighty-two year old Massachusetts patient collects a prescription and says nothing about the label. The pharmacy's policy is to print all labels in its standard size. A second patient the same day asks for larger directions because of impaired vision. What does the statute require?

choices.text: Nothing for the first patient; typed directions at no more than ten characters per inch for the second.
Enlarged directions for both, since the first patient is plainly elderly.
Nothing for either, because the statute governs the pharmacy's own type standard.
Enlarged directions for the second patient only if a prescriber orders them.
Enlarged print across the entire label for the second patient, not the directions alone.

comparison.stem: A trained Massachusetts pharmacist has Vivitrol in stock and a patient asks for an injection today. There is no patient-specific prescription or prescriber direction for this dose. What is the best action under the MH/SUD administration guidance?

choices.text: Administer because Vivitrol appears on the eligible-medication list.
Administer if the patient signs a pharmacy consent form.
Do not administer until the required patient-specific prescription/prescriber direction is in place.
Convert the stock dose into an OTC medication.
Ask a technician to select the dose and administer it independently.

comparison.stem: A ketamine prescription is presented to a Massachusetts community pharmacy. Which statements must be considered? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Ketamine is Schedule II and cannot be refilled.
Massachusetts treats ketamine as Schedule VI.
Schedule III refill limits apply to authorized refills.
Covered outpatient dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
Its anesthetic indication does not change Schedule III status.

comparison.stem: A pharmacy's DEA registrant wants a staff pharmacist to sign paper DEA Forms 222 when the registrant is away. The staff pharmacist is not the person who signed the pharmacy's most recent DEA registration application. Which arrangement can lawfully provide signing authority?

choices.text: A verbal instruction from the pharmacy manager made before each order, with no retained authorization record.
A notation in the pharmacy's employee handbook stating that every licensed pharmacist may sign Form 222 automatically.
Use of the registrant's CSOS password to sign the paper form electronically.
A supplier's written permission authorizing the staff pharmacist to sign the purchaser's order forms.
A compliant power of attorney granted by the registrant and retained so it is available for inspection.

comparison.stem: A newly registered pharmacy begins dispensing operations on Monday but has no controlled substances in stock. Its first controlled-substance shipment is expected on Friday. What should the pharmacist in charge do about the federal initial inventory?

choices.text: Wait until Friday and treat the arriving shipment record as the initial inventory.
Create the initial inventory on Monday and record that no controlled substances are then on hand.
Do not create an initial inventory because the requirement begins only after a controlled substance is received.
Ask the wholesaler to create the pharmacy's initial inventory when the first order is shipped.
Use the first biennial inventory as both the initial inventory and the record of Friday's shipment.

comparison.stem: Before a pharmacy deploys medications through a Massachusetts ADD, which actions support the required product integrity and inventory accountability? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Use manufacturer-sealed original packaging or compliant repackaging for a single dose/person
Reconcile ADD inventory activity against what the pharmacy sent or expects to receive
Track access and transaction activity so discrepancies can be investigated
Report medication losses according to the applicable pharmacy licensing-body requirements.
Delete access records after each shift once the cabinet count appears correct

comparison.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy with two separate dispensing windows is reviewing its counseling-rights signage. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A single sign at the store entrance satisfies the requirement for the whole pharmacy.
The letters may be any size provided the sign is legible from the counter.
A sign must be posted conspicuously adjacent to each area where prescriptions are dispensed.
The sign must be at least 11 inches in height by 14 inches in width.
The sign must be printed in both English and Spanish.

comparison.stem: A methylphenidate Schedule II prescription is issued for an LTCF resident and the pharmacy will partially fill it over time under the federal special pathway. What maximum time framework applies from the prescription's issue date, unless it is discontinued sooner?

choices.text: A 72-hour partial-fill window
A 7-day partial-fill window
A 90-day partial-fill window
A 60-day period measured from the prescription issue date
A 6-month partial-fill window

comparison.stem: A newly registered pharmacy begins dispensing operations on Monday but has no controlled substances in stock. Its first controlled-substance shipment is expected on Friday. What should the pharmacist in charge do about the federal initial inventory?

choices.text: Wait until Friday and treat the arriving shipment record as the initial inventory.
Create the initial inventory on Monday and record that no controlled substances are then on hand.
Do not create an initial inventory because the requirement begins only after a controlled substance is received.
Ask the wholesaler to create the pharmacy's initial inventory when the first order is shipped.
Use the first biennial inventory as both the initial inventory and the record of Friday's shipment.

comparison.stem: On Friday morning, a pharmacy discovers a significant unexplained loss of controlled substances. The investigation cannot be completed that day. Which federal response is correct?

choices.text: Wait for the investigation before contacting DEA.
Give oral notice within 24 hours and take no further action.
File Form 106 within one business day instead of separate notice.
Send written DEA notice within one business day and Form 106 within 45 calendar days.
Notify only the Massachusetts Board because the loss occurred in Massachusetts.
